abstract: We have investigated the quantitative and qualitative attributes of a scanning quadrupole data-independent acquisition (ZT Scan DIA) mode enabled on a SCIEX ZenoTOF 7600+ system using nanoflow chromatographic separations and targeted towards immunopeptidomic analysis. ZT Scan DIA incorporates increased ion utilization and MS/MS sensitivity introduced through the Zeno trapping modality, with quadrupole-resolved isolation windows in the data-independent acquisition mode. We demonstrate superior quantitative performance of ZT Scan DIA in sensitive nanoflow separations of tryptic peptides. Additionally, in LFQBench experiments, we demonstrate a remarkable quantitative accuracy and precision with experimentally measured precursor false-discovery rates below 1% using complex mixtures of yeast, human, and E. coli-derived tryptic digests when compared to conventional DIA experiments on the same platform. Having established its effectiveness in nanoflow proteomics analyses, we further investigated ZT Scan DIA for HLA-peptide characterization. These analyses highlighted the ability of the scanning quadrupole dimension to enrich the information needed for improved fragment-to-precursor assignment and quantitation of near-isobaric immunopeptides, should the search algorithms exploit it.
